claims.claim_ar: تقديم السّيئة (بِالسَّيِّئَةِ) قبل الحَسنة (الْحَسَنَةِ) لإبراز استعجال الناس للسّيئة مقابل تأخير الله للعقوبة
claims.claim_en: Taqdīm/takhīr (presentation/delay): the bad (al-sayyi'ah) is placed before the good (al-hasanah) to highlight people's haste for the bad in contrast with God's postponing of punishment.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Emphasizes human impatience and immediacy of perceived harm, setting up a contrast with divine forbearance.

claims.claim_ar: مقابلة وتكرار عبر «وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ ...» لعرض صفتَي الرحمة (المغفرة) مقابل الشدة (العقاب)
claims.claim_en: Muqābalah (contrast): the repeated formula 'and indeed your Lord...' presents the attributes of forgiveness versus severe punishment in opposition.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Creates tension between hope and fear — consolation through mercy immediately balanced by warning of punishment.

claims.claim_ar: تِباق (تضاد) بين «مَغْفِرَةٍ» و«شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ» يضع صفتَي التراحم والعقاب كقوتين متقابلتين في نفس السياق البياني
claims.claim_en: Tibāq (antithesis): the pairing of 'forgiveness' and 'severe punishment' places mercy and retribution as opposing forces within the same context.
claims.needs_review_reason: Tibaq vs muqabalah classifications overlap here; reviewer may decide which badi subtype is primary.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Heightens moral ambivalence and urgency: believers are given both hope and a stern reminder.

claims.claim_ar: التفات في الخطاب من مخاطبة الرسول (وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ) إلى بيان عام ووقائع سابقة («وَقَدْ خَلَتْ...») — تغيير منظور يخدم التعميم والتوكيد
claims.claim_en: Iltifāt (shift in address): the verse moves from addressing the Prophet ('you') to making a general statement about past peoples, shifting viewpoint to generalize and emphasize the point.
claims.needs_review_reason: Source citation discusses similar rhetorical shift in commentary on other verses; mapping to this verse is interpretive and should be checked.
claims.rhetorical_effect: The shift broadens the reproach from an individual addressee to a universal lesson, increasing the didactic force.
